newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MIM SAYS COAL BEATS GAS FOR GENERATION.
newsitem.headline: MIM SAYS COAL BEATS GAS FOR GENERATION.

text.p: Base metals and coal mining giant MIM Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday that coal, not gas, should be used for base-load power generation in Queensland.
"Gas should be applied where it can add more value - as an industrial feedstock, in peak load generation and in particular locations such as Mount Isa," MIM chief executive said.

"Gas is not so plentiful that it should be used for large-scale base load power generation," he told an Australian Gas Association meeting. "In south-east Queensland and central Queensland where most electricity is required in this state, coal is less than half the cost of gas into power stations."

Stump said gas was competitive in the base metals mining centre of Mount Isa to generate electricity from the Mica Creek power station only because of the remote area to which coal must be hauled. Also, gas replacement and additional generating sets were much less expensive than coal for that area, he said.
MIM's former Mount Isa coal-fired power station is shortly to be converted to gas with the group selling an 80 percent interest in Mica Creek to Austa North West Power Pty Ltd.
A gas pipeline is now under construction and gas expected to be delivered next year, Stump said.
"Nevertheless, in the enthusiasm to expand the use of gas, we should remember two things," Stump said.
"First, coal is a considerably more abundant and cheaper source of energy than gas and we have plenty of coal in Australia, especially in Queensland," he said.
"Secondly, clean coal technologies have improved and continue to improve both the efficiency and the environmental performance of coal," Stump said.

Stump said a study by the Australian Gas Association, while referring to more than adequate total gas reserves in Australia to meet demands, predicted a supply shortage in the eastern states, possibly within four years.

"Only half the world's population has access to electricty. Coal reserves are the world's most significant fossil fuel resource," he said. "We should use this vast and economical resource to generate the bulk of our electricity in Australia and to supply our low sulphur coals to other countries."
However, Stump said he looked forward to a period of greater use of gas and increasing efficiency in the use of Australia's gas reserves.
